title: Armenia National Adaptation Funding Facility (Adaptation Fund locally led adaptation grant, AF00000360)
summary: A four-year Adaptation Fund facility that EPIU would run to pay for small community-led climate adaptation projects in Armenia's regions and municipalities. It also sets up Regional Climate Adaptation Committees, carries out regional climate vulnerability assessments and trains local officials. The Adaptation Fund project page lists the proposal as approved; it records no start date yet.
activities: Component 1 (USD 300,000): regional climate vulnerability assessments; translating the National Adaptation Plan and sector plans into region-specific action plans; setting up Regional Climate Adaptation Committees; training 500 regional and municipal officials
Component 2 (USD 500,000): stakeholder mapping and needs assessment, capacity building, knowledge-sharing platforms and networking events

Component 3 (USD 3.8 million): identify, appraise and grant-finance community-led adaptation sub-projects through calls for small project proposals, e.g. drought-tolerant crops and drip irrigation, climate-smart livestock and pasture management, small water harvesting ponds and reservoirs, watershed restoration, reforestation and wetland rehabilitation, climate-resilient buildings and urban drainage, community early-warning systems, solar-powered pumps, small disaster-preparedness infrastructure
Indicative sequence in the proposal: months 1-6 vulnerability assessments, months 7-12 sub-project prioritisation, months 13-36 sub-project execution
results: Mid-term milestone (end of year 2): 5 regions, 25 communities, 25 adaptation projects, 250 stakeholders (100 women), 5 knowledge products, 100,000 direct beneficiaries (at least 40% women)
End-of-project target: 10 regions, 50 communities, 50 adaptation projects, 500 stakeholders (200 women), 10 knowledge products, 200,000 direct beneficiaries (at least 40% women)
stage: Adaptation Fund proposal approved; implementation start not yet recorded on the Fund's project page

title: Building Nature-Positive Future for Lake Sevan (GEF-8 / Global Biodiversity Framework Fund, ADB)
summary: A small GEF-8 grant from the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund, to be implemented through ADB with the Ministry of Environment, to support Lake Sevan's environmental sustainability and green infrastructure. It would pay for feasibility, investment planning, engineering design and due diligence for priority sanitation investments that address wastewater-related nutrient and pollution pressure on the lake. It prepares the larger ADB investment programme described in the separate Lake Sevan wastewater record.
activities: Feasibility studies and investment planning for priority sanitation investments around Lake Sevan
Engineering design and due diligence for those investments (wastewater-related nutrient and pollution pressures)
Support to Lake Sevan's environmental sustainability and green infrastructure
stage: GEF concept (PIF) approved; CEO endorsement and start date not yet recorded

title: Lake Sevan Basin Wastewater Management investment programme (ADB-supported; proposed ADB loan 60183-001, Lake Sevan Environmental Viability and Advanced Green Engineering Project)
summary: A planned multi-stage programme to stop untreated and poorly treated wastewater from reaching Lake Sevan by upgrading the existing treatment plants of Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis with biological treatment, then building plants in medium-sized towns and small plants for rural communities. The Public Investment Committee approved the three-stage programme on 1 July 2026, and ADB is preparing a proposed USD 100 million loan. The total programme cost is reported as USD 260 million and the programme is still in design.
activities: Stage 1: upgrade the existing wastewater treatment plants (currently mechanical treatment only) in Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis and add biological treatment
Stage 2: build new treatment plants in medium-sized agglomerations of the Sevan basin
Stage 3: build small stand-alone plants for isolated and small rural communities
Sewerage network expansion: feasibility work (June 2025) foresaw network design of up to 570 km in the basin and decentralised solutions for sewage that is not connected
results: Phosphorus discharge into the lake may fall by up to 70 tonnes a year (news.am, 2 Sep 2026, projection)
Feasibility scenario (Hetq, 14 Jun 2025): the more centralised model would route up to 65% of the basin's sewage to the three plants; the less centralised model up to 35%
stage: Three-stage programme approved by the Public Investment Committee (1 July 2026); first-phase investment package reported approved; programme in design phase; ADB loan listed as 'Proposed'

title: Armenia Reservoir and Irrigation System Enhancement (ARISE): feasibility study for new reservoirs at Getik, Karmir Gyugh and Garnahovit (ADB)
summary: ADB-supported programme to prepare three new irrigation reservoirs at Getik, Karmir Gyugh and Garnahovit. A consulting agreement for an eight-month feasibility study was signed around May 2025, and an investment package is to go to the Public Investment Committee after the study. Construction dates and financing for the reservoirs themselves are not published.
activities: Techno-economic assessment of the three reservoirs
Environmental and social impact analysis
Basin (watershed) management and modernisation of the downstream irrigation systems
Preparation of an investment package for the Public Investment Committee
results: About 3,500 farmers are expected to gain better water access and higher agricultural productivity (Water Committee news, 2 May 2025)
stage: Feasibility study under way or just finished; investment package for the Public Investment Committee to follow; study result not found

title: Government of Armenia Programme 2026-2031: water, irrigation, Lake Sevan and forest commitments
summary: The Government's five-year programme sets national targets for new reservoirs, irrigation, Lake Sevan restoration and afforestation. It is a policy commitment rather than a funded project, and the source gives no budget or lender. It is useful for coordination because it shows where donor programmes are expected to be asked to contribute.
activities: Start construction of 10 reservoirs, with completion targeted for 2033
Construct and reconstruct 350 km of canals and pipelines
Introduce an ecosystem-based management model for Lake Sevan and its catchment, including river-ecosystem and biodiversity restoration
Clear forest plantations flooded by Lake Sevan; reduce pollution and improve waste collection on the lake's shore; return illegally occupied areas of Sevan National Park
Carry out afforestation and reforestation; provide 24/7 forest and protected-area protection through the Ecopatrol Service
Cap abstraction from the Ararat Artesian Basin at the legal sustainable yield; promote water efficiency and river-ecosystem protection; introduce a carbon-pricing system (no date)
results: 350 km of canals and pipelines built or reconstructed
Irrigation for 10,000 ha of new agricultural land
24-hour water supply in Yerevan, Gyumri and Vanadzor (no date given)
Ararat Artesian Basin abstraction capped at 926 million m3 a year
At least 100 ha of forest plantations flooded by Lake Sevan cleared; Lake Sevan water quality brought to at least 'good' status (no dates)
About 10,000 ha of afforestation and reforestation (no date given)
stage: Government programme adopted (announcement-level commitments); no project-level budgets or financing in the source

title: Armenia Water Compact 2036: national commitments for water security reform (Water Committee)
summary: A ten-year national water-security commitment issued by the Water Committee, setting outcome targets for irrigation, drinking water and sanitation, groundwater and Lake Sevan protection, and flood and drought risk. It lists priority investments and reforms but no projects, sites or budget. It is the framework that donor water programmes (World Bank WISE, AFD/EU WAIDA, EBRD, ADB) are expected to fit into.
activities: Rehabilitate and modernise irrigation infrastructure to cut water losses and energy use; pilot performance-based contracts and blended finance for irrigation
Rehabilitate and extend drinking-water networks, focusing on rural and underserved communities; expand wastewater collection and treatment; prepare a pipeline of bankable wastewater investments
Flood and drought risk reduction and storage reliability, including rehabilitating existing reservoirs and, where justified, building new small and medium-sized reservoirs
Real-time monitoring and a national water informatics system; automated monitoring of Lake Sevan withdrawals; stop over-abstraction in the Ararat Artesian Basin

Reforms: Irrigation Strategy, Water Supply and Sanitation Strategy, National Water Resources Management Strategy, Water Sector Master Plan, Water Code revision, tariff reform, support to Water User Associations and to Jrar, basin management plans for the six Basin Management Areas
results: By 2036: water losses in priority irrigation systems down about 50% and energy use for irrigation down about 30%
By 2036: about 200,000 ha of priority irrigation infrastructure modernised; about 250,000-300,000 people with improved irrigation services
By 2036: safely managed drinking water for about 95% of residents (about 2.7 million people); sanitation for about 60% (about 1.4 million people)
By 2036: about 60% of municipal wastewater safely treated; municipal non-revenue water cut to about 45% (from about 55% in 2024)
By 2036: flood and drought risk management improved for about 1.2 million people; digital climate advice and early warning for at least 300,000 water users
stage: National commitment document published in 2026; sector strategies and master plan still to be developed and approved; no project financing attached

title: Biodiversity Conservation Targets of the Republic of Armenia and Action Plan 2026-2030 (Minister of Environment Order No. 100-L)
summary: National biodiversity plan with five goals and 30 targets under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, approved by the Minister of Environment. Only the forest-related targets could be read: restoring degraded forest ecosystems, raising forest cover and cutting fuelwood demand by 2030. The plan names no budget, donors or regions.
activities: Restore degraded forest ecosystems and enhance climate resilience of forest landscapes by 2030
Promote climate-resilient forest management practices; reduce community fuelwood demand
Introduce global indicators and criteria for sustainable forest management (2026-2029)
Promote non-chemical disease control in ArmForest SNCO forest enterprises (2026-2028)
results: Target 2: restore at least 15,000 ha of degraded forest ecosystems by 2030
Target 10: increase forest cover by 12,500 ha and cut community fuelwood demand by at least 30% by 2030
stage: National targets and action plan approved by ministerial order in 2026; funding and implementing partners not stated

title: EU4Green Recovery East: preliminary Flood Risk Management Plan for the Debed River Basin (Armenia)
summary: A small planned study under the EU's regional EU4Green Recovery East programme to prepare a preliminary flood risk management plan for the Debed River Basin, helping Armenia align with the EU Floods Directive. It would produce a preliminary flood risk assessment, flood hazard and flood risk maps for one pilot area, and a draft plan. The pilot area is not named.
activities: Preliminary flood risk assessment for the Debed River Basin
Flood hazard maps for a pilot area, including hydrological and hydraulic modelling
Flood risk maps and vulnerability assessment for the same pilot area
Draft preliminary Flood Risk Management Plan for the Debed River Basin, aligned with EU Floods Directive 2007/60/EC
stage: Consultancy tender published 23 Feb 2026 (deadline 13 Mar 2026); award and start not found

title: UNDP / Ministry of Environment concept notes for climate-resilient irrigation and flood/transport infrastructure (loss and damage)
summary: UNDP and the Ministry of Environment are preparing two project concepts to attract international climate finance for climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure and for flood-resilient and transport infrastructure. In September 2025 they were presented to ministries, the Water Committee, ADB and FAO to explore funding sources and next steps. No amounts, locations or targets have been published.
activities: Co-development of theories of change for both concepts (workshop 17-18 June 2025)
Presentation and discussion of the two concepts with ministries, the Water Committee, Armhydromet, EPIU, ADB and FAO to explore financing sources and steps from design to implementation (18 Sep 2025)
stage: Two project concepts under preparation (theories of change drafted June 2025; presented to partners 18 Sep 2025); no submission to a fund found
